description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy for two metrics—Δ Accuracy and Initial Accuracy—across a range of initial confidence values from 0.86 to 1.00. The x-axis, labeled "Initial Confidence," is a linear scale with tick marks at intervals of 0.02, ranging from 0.86 to 1.00. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," is also a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with major tick marks at 0.2 intervals. The blue line, representing Δ Accuracy, starts at an accuracy of approximately 0.92 when the initial confidence is 0.86, rises slightly to a peak of about 0.98 at an initial confidence of 0.97, and then gradually declines to around 0.96 at an initial confidence of 1.00. The green line, representing Initial Accuracy, begins at an accuracy of approximately 0.68 at an initial confidence of 0.86, increases to a peak of about 0.98 at an initial confidence of 0.97, and then decreases to around 0.78 at an initial confidence of 1.00. The orange line, representing Δ Accuracy, starts at an accuracy of approximately 0.32 at an initial confidence of 0.86, decreases to a minimum of about 0.02 at an initial confidence of 0.95, and then increases to approximately 0.24 at an initial confidence of 1.00. Error bars are present for all data points, indicating variability in the measurements.
